selected_trajectory.question: Did the late-2022 participant judgment that container freight rates had peaked and begun normalising precede a later 2023 outcome of materially lower freight rates and earnings as congestion eased and market conditions normalised?
selected_trajectory.scope_guard: This is one normalization-clock trajectory. It does not open a contract-basis trajectory, an inventory-only trajectory, P147, or a second pilot.

historical_reality.planned_claim: Maersk reported moderating logistics demand, easing supply bottlenecks, and quarter-on-quarter declines in freight and charter rates during Q3 2022.

contemporaneous_judgment.speaker: Soren Skou, CEO of A.P. Moller - Maersk
contemporaneous_judgment.planned_claim: Maersk judged that Ocean freight rates had peaked and started to normalise, and expected Ocean earnings to decline in coming periods.

later_outcome.planned_claim: Maersk's 2023 reporting showed a large decline in average Ocean freight rates and profitability after market normalisation and easing congestion; Hapag-Lloyd independently reported a similarly large fall in its 2023 average freight rate.

claim_plan.no_lookahead_rule: The 2023 outcome sources are invisible at the 2022-11-02 cutoff and may only appear at a later cutoff after their own first-known dates.
